# A frozen NOW in the data-sync spec ages into a permanent CI red

## Context

`Engine Tests` is red on `dev` at `5ae9358063` (run 33624118983), so the `unit` job now fails on every branch and every PR is gated — including the demo chain (#18059, #18063).

This is **not** the three PRs merged this morning: #18066, #18061 and #18068 each had `gh pr checks` exit 0 at review time. It crossed over during the following hour.

It is also **not** the production corpus guard misbehaving. That guard is working exactly as designed, and the `Data Sync Pipeline` workflow failing is the finding it exists to surface — already tracked by #17920 (the GitHub corpus stage lost in the devindex split) with the staleness alarm on #17834. Nothing here should quiet that.

## The Problem

`test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/dataSyncPipeline.spec.mjs:17-18` derives every fixture date from a frozen constant:

```js
NOW   = new Date('2026-08-31T12:00:00Z'),
hours = n => new Date(NOW.getTime() - n * 3_600_000).toISOString(),
```

The pure-function arms are hermetic because they hand that same constant to the subject — `assertCorpusFreshness({facetCommitDates, now: NOW})`.

The **RUN-path** arms under `test.describe('the refusal reaches the RUN path, not only the pure function')` are not. They call `emitGeneratedData`, which invokes `assertCorpusFreshness({facetCommitDates})` with no `now`, so the subject falls back to `new Date()` — the real clock — while the fixture date stays pinned to 2026-08-31.

The measured age is therefore `realNow − 2026-08-31T11:00Z`, not the injected value:

| | injected | measured at 2026-09-02T11:21Z |
|---|---|---|
| `runWith({corpusAgeHours: 1})` | 1h | **48.35h** |

against a 48h threshold — which is the `48.4h` in the failure text, to the decimal:

```
Error: dataSyncPipeline: refusing to derive the portal from a stale corpus —
  `issues` is 48.4h old (threshold 48h), `pulls` is 48.4h old (threshold 48h),
  `discussions` is 48.4h old (threshold 48h)
    at assertCorpusFreshness (buildScripts/dataSyncPipeline.mjs:705:15)
    at emitGeneratedData (buildScripts/dataSyncPipeline.mjs:781:13)
    at test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/dataSyncPipeline.spec.mjs:320:13
```

So `a fresh corpus lets the derivation stage run` has not been testing a fresh corpus since it was written. It passed for ~48 hours because the wall clock happened to sit inside the threshold of its own frozen constant, and it is now permanently red and worsening — the gap grows an hour per hour.

The sibling arm (`a stale corpus stops the derivation stage from running at all`, `corpusAgeHours: 120`) still passes, but for the wrong reason: it asserts a refusal, and it now gets one whatever the fixture says. It has stopped discriminating.

## The Architectural Reality

- `buildScripts/dataSyncPipeline.mjs:697` — `assertCorpusFreshness({facetCommitDates, maxAgeHours, now = new Date()})` already exposes `now` as a seam.
- `buildScripts/dataSyncPipeline.mjs:781` — `emitGeneratedData` calls it **without** `now`, which is correct for production and is what leaves the RUN path clock-dependent under test.
- `test/.../dataSyncPipeline.spec.mjs:285` — `runWith` stubs `execute` so any `git` call returns `hours(corpusAgeHours)`. The stub works; the constant it is built from is the defect.

Introduced by #17938 (`A missing emission stage or a stale corpus must fail the run`), which added both guards and these arms.

## The Fix

Make the RUN-path arms hermetic. The fixture date must be relative to whatever clock the subject will read, so an injected age is the measured age.

Smallest correct change: give the RUN-path harness a real-clock-relative helper rather than the frozen `NOW`, leaving the pure-function arms and their pinned `NOW` exactly as they are. Production is untouched, so the Data Sync workflow keeps failing loudly and #17920 stays visible.

The alternative — threading a `now` seam through `emitGeneratedData` — is rejected here: it widens a production signature for test convenience when the subject already exposes the seam one level down, and the harness is the thing that is wrong.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `a fresh corpus lets the derivation stage run` passes regardless of wall-clock date, verified by running it with the system clock unchanged and again against a date well past the current threshold window.
- [ ] The refusal arm is restored to a discriminating test: it must fail if the guard stops refusing, rather than passing on a refusal it would now get anyway. Red-first evidence required — mutate `assertCorpusFreshness` to never throw and show that arm going red.
- [ ] No change to `buildScripts/dataSyncPipeline.mjs`; the production guard's behaviour and the `Data Sync Pipeline` workflow's failure are unchanged and still surface #17920.
- [ ] `npm run test-unit` green on `dev`.
- [ ] A note in the spec naming why the RUN-path arms cannot share the pinned `NOW`, so the next author does not re-freeze them.

## Out of Scope

- Restoring the corpus stage or any part of #17920 — the production red is correct and must remain.
- The staleness alarm on #17834.
- Changing the 48h threshold. The threshold is not the problem and lowering or raising it would only move the bomb.
